record.original_question: For each unpredictably emergent Costas-array construction method obtained by adding one or more dots to an existing Costas array, determine whether there is a finite threshold N beyond which that method never produces a Costas array of order n > N.

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Determine the scope of the unpredictably emergent construction techniques discussed in Section 3.2. In particular, is it the case that, for each method amongst them, a N ∈ N can be found, such that this method produces no Costas arrays of order n > N?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n×n permutation matrix (equivalently, a permutation f:{1,...,n}→{1,...,n}) such that all the n(n−1)/2 displacement vectors between distinct pairs of its dots are pairwise distinct; equivalently, for every nonzero integer h with |h|<n, the function i ↦ f(i+h)−f(i) is injective on its domain.

A "dot-addition" construction method is a deterministic procedure that takes a Costas array A of order m as input, augments it by adjoining one or more new dots (e.g., placed at corner positions or otherwise) to form an (m+k)×(m+k) permutation matrix B, and outputs B whenever B happens to satisfy the Costas property. Such a method is called unpredictably emergent if there is no known sufficient condition, depending only on m (or on m together with auxiliary parameters), guaranteeing in advance that the augmented array B will be Costas; whether B is Costas must be verified a posteriori. Several specific unpredictably emergent methods of this kind are known (for instance, single corner-dot additions to Welch–Rickard or Golomb–Rickard arrays, as well as analogous two-dot or interior-dot variants).

Problem. For each such unpredictably emergent dot-addition construction method M, decide whether there exists a finite threshold N = N(M) ∈ ℕ such that M produces no Costas array of any order n > N. Equivalently, determine for each method M whether the set of orders n for which M yields at least one Costas array is finite, and if so, exhibit such a bound.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of bounding the orders of Costas arrays produced by unpredictably emergent dot-addition methods remains open. Exhaustive computer searches have verified that several such methods (e.g., the Rickard-type constructions) yield no new Costas arrays up to order 300, but no proof of a finite cutoff N for any of these methods is known. The problem is listed among open problems in the Costas-array literature and surveys.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in Costas arrays
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 11 asks whether for each unpredictably emergent construction method an N can be found such that the method produces no Costas arrays of order n>N.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly posed as an open problem regarding the scope of unpredictably emergent dot-addition methods.

status_evidence.title: Costas array - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Known sporadic constructions and emergent variants are documented; no general proof of a finite cutoff for emergent methods is reported.
status_evidence.claim: No known proof establishes a finite threshold for unpredictably emergent constructions.

status_evidence.title: Costas Arrays: Survey, Standardization, and MATLAB Toolbox
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Costas array constructions including emergent ones; reports exhaustive enumeration up to moderate orders without new emergent arrays beyond known small instances.
status_evidence.claim: Empirical evidence shows no new emergent arrays for these methods up to high orders, but no theoretical bound is proved.
